name: Alexander Tsai
about:
I'm a machine learning engineer at TikTok, working on detecting AI content and interpretability. I was previously with ExodusPoint, developing quantitative strategies for credit default swaps.

I am interested in how we can better understand the inner workings behind various multimodal models, particularly within the domains of AI safety and robotics.

In my spare time, I [write blogs](/blog/) and program drones. Connect with me on [X](https://x.com/alexyrtsai) to see more!

experience.title: Machine Learning Engineer Intern
experience.summary: Developed an **AI-generated image classifier** with **99.85% precision and 76% recall** on production data. Experiments were focused around generalization to out-of-distribution data, robustness to compression, and visual interpretability (the hardest part).

experience.title: Quantitative Research Intern
experience.summary: Worked primarily on credit markets. I explored several potential approaches towards credit world models. Some interesting questions: what features should we model on levels vs changes? How can we numerically represent certain events e.g. the fed announcing a rate hike?

experience.title: Machine Learning Engineer Intern
experience.summary: Built and deployed a content moderation pipeline with **Qwen3-VL and XGBoost**. Focused heavily on improving visual understanding for VLMs through RL (GRPO) and optimizing inference (speculative decoding, batching, multithreading) for large-scale offline processing.

experience.title: Data Science Intern
experience.summary: Built an **XGBoost** transaction-cost model for mortgage-backed securities over 5 years of trade data. Hyperparameter optimization and feature engineering with SHAP graphs reduced **RMSE by 21%** over baseline.

research.title: Research Fellow
research.summary: Developed a **multilingual RAG chatbot** with LangChain and Firestore to enhance the financial literacy of migrant workers. The [published findings](https://reachalliance.org/reports/how-can-we-utilise-conversational-a-i-to-enhance-financial-literacy-for-migrant-workers-in-singapore/) were presented at a University of Toronto conference and in a [TEDx talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3C1R1JlOQEk).

research.title: AI for Youth Instructor
research.summary: Taught **Python, statistics, and neural networks** to 30 students in Intel’s AI for Youth program. Guided six teams on capstone projects, including computer vision attendance systems and emotional-support chatbots.

education.detail: Visiting student, Global Computing and Data Science Program

talks.title: Financial Literacy for Migrant Workers Through Conversational AI
talks.venue: Reach Alliance report · University of Toronto conference

projects.note: Built with my friends Lily and Stella at Cal Hacks 2026! Stella is a tool to autonomously identify workflow patterns and automate tasks for users unfamiliar with AI.
